subject: GPU pledge validation for Shearwater - sizing + fallback plan
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex@shearwater.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production sizing request + provisional pledge

Hi David,

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday — we’re excited to move Shearwater’s inference off-prem and into Redwood Dedicated for our US launch. Per the roadmap, we expect to go live with v1 on 2027-01-20 and need an initial dedicated capacity plan for the first 90 days. Top-level numbers:

- Peak concurrent requests: 320 live sessions (p99 concurrency spike planning)
- Avg prompt length: ~900 tokens; response avg 600 tokens
- Model: open-gpt-xl-30B (we may accept a 12-bit quantized variant)
- Latency target: 250ms p95 for interactive endpoints

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provision a provisional pledge for the month of January (approx 32 A100-equivalent GPUs) and what fallback/quantization options we should expect?

I’ve attached our forecast sheet and a draft MOU to speed the legal/procurement loop. If you can give us a short internal note (what you can commit now vs what needs procurement signoff), that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Li
Head of Platform, Shearwater AI
Attachments: Shearwater_Sizing_P0_v2.xlsx, MOU_gpu_terms.pdf
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@shearwater.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production sizing request + provisional pledge

Alex — thanks for the clear numbers and the attachments. I’ve looped in Stephanie (sales lead), Karthik (capacity & infra), and Monica (customer success/provisioning) so we can turn this into a concrete provisional commitment and run the availability check. Quick answers up front:

- Short answer: we can provision a provisional pledge now for January for the ballpark you listed, subject to procurement and final MOU sign-off.
- What we need from you: final expected concurrency profile by hour for the first 30 days (you can drop that on the Drive link), and confirmation if you will accept 12-bit q4_0 quantization for a smaller memory footprint.

Karthik — can you run an inventory and feasibility check (node mapping, expected throughput per A100-equivalent, and a fallback plan if we need to route to a smaller variant) and advise on how many dedicated GPUs we should soft-reserve? Please also include the minimum reservation period we’d ask Shearwater to commit to for a reserved pool vs a soft hold.

Monica — once Karthik confirms numbers, can you prepare the mutual action plan & a procurement checklist (DocuSign + billing contact) so Alex’s procurement team has everything they need to sign quickly?

Alex — copied you on the internal ask; we’ll get a capacity note back within 24 business hours.

—David
David Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 14:32:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Production sizing request + provisional pledge

David / team — ran a quick feasibility snapshot against current fleet and upcoming maintenance windows. Summary and recommended options below (assumes open-gpt-xl-30B baseline):

1) Raw capacity estimate (conservative):
- 30 A100-equivalent GPUs gives ~280 concurrent sessions at target latency with continuous batching enabled (KV cache warm).
- 32 GPUs is reasonable as a safety buffer for expected surge; 32 is our recommended provisional pledge.

2) Quantization/fallback options:
- If Shearwater accepts 12-bit quantized model (q4_0), we can fit the model into fewer GPUs (approx -20% GPU memory footprint) which would reduce the provisional pledge to ~26 GPUs while preserving p95 latency within 300ms.
- As a rapid fallback, we can route 15% of traffic to a smaller 13B variant in early hours to protect tail latency during spikes.

3) Reservation mechanics:
- Soft hold: we can place a soft hold (reserving capacity in our scheduler without billing) for up to six weeks. Soft holds guarantee capacity unless there is a force-major reallocation; they require sign-off from Capacity Ops.
- Reserved pool (contracted): requires a 3-month minimum billing commitment and procurement sign-off, but gives hard isolation and SLA.

4) Ops impact & blockers:
- We have a maintenance blackout 2026-12-24 -> 2027-01-02 in us-west; scheduling the commit before the blackout reduces risk for the Jan 20 launch.
- Need finalization of model quant (q4_0 vs fp16) and target p95 latency to size exact mem footprints.

Recommended next steps (short):
- Alex: confirm quantization tolerance + share hourly concurrency profile for first 30 days.
- David/Stephanie: approve a 32-GPU soft hold pending procurement (monica will prepare docs).
- Ops (Karthik): if approved, we’ll place a soft hold and tag nodes for Shearwater; we’ll produce a runbook with fallback routing rules.

Runbook link: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/sizing/DW-2026-1197 (internal)

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@shearwater.ai>, procurement@shearwater.ai
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production sizing request + provisional pledge

Alex / Shearwater procurement team — thanks for the prompt details and for agreeing to evaluate q4_0 quant. Per Karthik’s note, Redwood can place a provisional 32-GPU soft hold for Shearwater to cover the January launch window. Conditions and next steps below:

1) Provisional commitment (soft hold): 32 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved in our us-west pool. Soft hold window: 2026-12-06 -> 2027-01-31. This is non-billable and intended to guarantee scheduling priority; final billing depends on whether you convert to a Reserved Pool.

2) Required inputs to finalize hold:
- Confirmation on model quant (q4_0 accepted? yes/no)
- Hourly concurrency profile for first 30 days (drop to our Drive folder)
- Signed MOU / procurement sheet (we’ve attached the MOU you provided with minor redlines)

3) Conversion path to Reserved Pool (optional):
- 3-month minimum contracted commit; procurement sign-off and DocuSign completion required. If you sign before 2026-12-20 we can guarantee rolling off the maintenance blackout risk window.

4) Fallback behavior:
- If spikes exceed capacity, Redwood will automatically route up to 15% of traffic to a 13B variant (as Karthik suggested) and apply KV-prefetch to reduce cold-starts. We’ll coordinate a canary for the routing change during low-traffic hours.

Monica will send the procurement checklist and a DocuSign link for the MOU now. Once Shearwater confirms quant and uploads concurrency profile, I’ll tell Karthik to activate the soft hold.

HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/DEAL-1197
DocuSign link (pending): https://www.docusign.com/sheerwater/DW-2026-1197
Drive (upload): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ShearwaterSizing

Looking forward to getting this locked in.

—David
David Kim
